VR DREAMING

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
How do you makes dreams come true when children can't leave the house? by bring the dreams to their hospital beds

Summary:
How do you help a terminally ill child reach for their dream when the world has become a death zone for them. Reach for a dream has turned to VR to support kids in hospital to reach their dreams from their hospital beds

Charlotte Maxeke is the first hospital where the project was rolled out. We will now be apart of the team bringing these amazing VR dreams to the children in the oncology unit at Baragwanath hospital

We will meet and get to know three children all at various stages of fighting cancer. All three families have basically been cut off from the outside world since COVID started, because their children are so Immune compromised. They can’t go out and play, they can’t have friends over, their world has just gotten smaller since March last year. But these terminally ill kids have such a way of always looking at the light, they put life into perspective in a way.

After we are allowed in to see a little bit of what it means for a child to fight every day to live, we will be witness to the first time they will go into this amazing VR dream world. They will swim with dolphins, hug puppies and run freely through an enchanted forest, in their minds they will be free for a minute. This will all happen from their hospital beds.


Further information:
All these kids have what they call life treatening illnesses, terminal basically

Xichavo Mhangani is 17 years old he has been diagnosed with Paratesticular Phabdomysarcoma (cancer)
Xichavo’s mother died in 2018 and his father is basically not involved in his life at all.He is doing matric this year and looking after his 2 siblings who are 14 and 10 years in a hired 2 rooms shack in Soweto depending on their support grant.He is basically a child headed family.
Cell no.:0734753221

Drew Wayne Olifant was diagnosed with Anaplastic Large cell Lymphoma he is 7 years old. He is the only child of a single mom. They live in Potchefstroom
Mom cell:0632517648


Hope Nyathi was diagnosed with L Distal Fermur Osteosarcoma, she is 15 years old. She lives with her mom and granny in Soweto. These kids have a 5 year survival rate and she was diagnosed 3 years ago
Mom cell: 0787144600

Script:


For 32 years Reach for a dream has been making the dreams of children with life threatening illnesses come true

RD:
we've never, not ever fulfilled the dream ever, ever.
In your three,
two years, ever
six dreams a day every day of the year.
As in 360 days a year.

But then COVID-19 hit South Africa and it became impossible to take immunocompromised children out into the real world

Katia : personally, I couldn't go out just because if I were to get sick from anybody else, even just the flu or anything like that, I would have to be taken to ICU and looked after, like, really intensely.
Genene
she wanted to go on Christmas to the ocean and because she loves the ocean and everything, but she couldn't go because she got ill and the doctors was too scared.
So she was crying a lot because she was couldn't wait to just put her feet in the ocean
Thato
I feel isolated sometimes because, well, we all scared of the pandemic, I'm scared that if I can get it, then I don't know what might happen to me because I'm not really safe around the whole thing.
Nicole:
they said if you found a genie's lamp and if you could ask for one wish, what would your wish be?
Sienna what happened if there was uncovered.

Mervin Serebro the chairman of reach for a dream and his team had to find new ways to safely keep these kids dreaming. So they brought in virtual reality
Verite up - cutest one - Siena
Using googles the Children can physically interact with these computer generated dream scapes. For 8 minutes they aren’t sick or in pain they are just kids

MERVIN: The technology today is so incredibly superior that you can almost put your hand out and touch the skin of an elephant.
So it does because that virtual world
enables those children. To to see or do almost anything,

Thato: I am in an enchanted forest
Wow the trees are huge

When Thato Moloi was diagnosed with Leukemia his bone marrow was already 90% full of cancer, he had to fight long and hard to come back from the brink

there are some chemo that I used to get, but they didn't treat me well. I remember this one chemo that we don't get along
My blood pressure was low. Then the doctor hurried up. She said that I must stay with her mother and leave her. She took something. They put something just to reverse the chemo. I don't know what it was. Then the doctor said that don't leave me because I could barely open my eyes. I was shutting down

Verite – some massive wow reaction! Thato

last year Chiqutta Breedt was diagnosed with blood cancer she was only 7 years old. it has been a long journey for both her and her mom genee

I think the hardest part, seeing your child go through all of this she seeing her helpless and you as a mother can't do anything for your child

VR - I see a Dolphin

I remember on a day she told me, you always makes me feel better. Why can't you do it now?
She asks, am I going to die? you can't tell. Like, I can't tell my child. I don't know.
And you don't know as a parent. You don't know in that situation.

Chiquitta: Can you touch the dolphin

In 2019 Katia Cignoli and her mom Sabina were diagnosed with cancer at almost the same time i. Sabina moved into the paediatric oncology ward and they went through Chemo together for most of last year

Katia interview 1 hospital
Did you ever feel like this was unfair, that this happened to you?
I did in the beginning, but then I learned to just accept it and move on.
I think it's just made me a stronger person.

Katia and mom 2
I think she was my strength in all of us. She's my little warrior. She gave me so much strength. And to see her so positive about it and everything that I had no option. I had no option.
Katie and mom 2
I just think that if something happens to you, it's happened for a reason. It's to make you a stronger person and it just things happen for a reason. So I just based all positive thoughts off of that and I just try to make the best of it.

VERITE OF KATIA: I am going over – something something the scared moment

Sienna Etzinger was 4 years old when she diagnosed with cancer, she has spent the past two years in and out of hospitals undergoing surgery and chemotherapy, which has meant that for the longest time the hospital has been her home and Her mom Nicole has been right there next to her

And I think out of anything the hardest thing I think CNN had to accept as a little girl was losing her hair.
Did you have long hair? You know, she did your time. And you show me, like, how long was your hair? Was it here? Was it longer?
It was like, yeah. And then it fell out. Who cut your hair?
Then she. Did you cut your hair? Yeah, she did.
She took the power and she shaved her own head.

Sienna, Chiquitta, Katia and Thato are all in remission, even though they will all still be in treatment for a while for now the cancer is under control. Reach for a dream has already set up VR dream experiences at Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg academic and Baragwanath hospital. Their goal is to have these VR dream kits in hospitals across the country by the end of the year


what difference this makes to the children that are suffering with these life threatening illnesses
It's now been proven, medically proven, that that positivity produces endorphins and unquestionably.
Enables recovery in specific situations


It just transports them to a place that they can't go to.
Genene
Give them hope that they can still do that, you know.
Katia:
And I think it really takes your mind off of all those bad thoughts that are in your head that when you're going through.
They're exploring, they're enjoying something that's completely just for them.
It's like for eight minutes they they're kids.

Some final VR upsound – thato
